units.function: Large embedded-Postgres and real-filesystem integration suite for Company Skill list/detail, bundled releases, versions, social/store metadata, imports, forks, desired-state resolution, missing-source reconciliation, runtime materialization, project scanning and managed rename.
units.dependencyDirection: Tests invoke companySkillService and folderService directly over real database schemas and temporary filesystem trees, with mocked network fetches. Route authorization, policy evaluation, real Connector activation and distributed/multi-process behavior are outside scope.
units.keyDataModels: CompanySkill and content versions, provenance/inventory/source status, bundled release/folder, User/Agent editor, star/comment, sharing/category/folder, fork lineage/reassignment, desired Skill/version, missing-source marker, runtime entry, ProjectWorkspace scan candidate/conflict and managed local directory.
units.lifecycle: Seed Company and source rows; refresh/list/project bounded projections; import/skip/rename/replace packages; version/edit/fork/reassign; retain or prune missing sources; recover/materialize runtime files; preview/import workspace candidates; rename managed Skills and clean old runtime paths.
units.testAssessment: The 56 behavior tests are broad and often high quality: exact bundled snapshot hashes, tenant/folder boundaries, reserved-key and script-package rejection, symlink escape denial, stale-key visibility, cross-company metadata non-leakage, version snapshots, selective scans and Agent key rewrites are explicit. Focused Vitest was run outside the sandbox with a fresh isolated home, but embedded PostgreSQL failed after five attempts and all 56 tests were skipped, so 0 runtime tests passed. Critical gaps remain for multi-process concurrency, filesystem/database crash recovery, target-directory races, content quotas, disguised executables, remote integrity, approval/responsibility, secret handling and cleanup receipts.
units.designRationale: Protect a rich Skills Studio lifecycle with end-to-end database/filesystem regressions while retaining compatibility with legacy rows, stale desired references and local developer workspaces.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs tested capability-package admission, immutable provenance, tenant-safe FDE workspace discovery, transactional publication, leased runtime activation/revocation and responsible human approval across managed-cloud and local Connector nodes.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT selected test matrices—not Paperclip schemas—for exact package hashes, reserved namespaces, canonical containment/symlink denial, stale desired-state visibility, version binding, same-source idempotence, selective preview/import, tenant metadata non-leakage and byte-for-byte runtime snapshots. Add adversarial concurrency, crash recovery, resource bombs, secret canaries, signature/digest, approval/data-egress and activation receipt tests before Company OS implementation.
units.responsibilityConflict: The suite intentionally fixes destructive read-time pruning, partial SKILL.md-only runtime recovery, unversioned rename and bulk Agent capability-key mutation without accountable human, approval, action digest or immutable activity evidence. It tests User/Agent attribution but not organizational responsibility.
evidence: focused Vitest: 1 file and 56 tests skipped after embedded PostgreSQL failed to start five times; 0 passed
securityFindings: Tests explicitly require list() to hard-delete a missing local Skill when no active Agent desires it, with no grace period, tombstone, approval or audit evidence.
Tests explicitly allow runtime recovery from stored SKILL.md while referenced files are missing, without requiring a degraded attestation or fail-closed readiness state.
Legacy/direct GitHub rows use floating main refs and tests expect fork/read fetches from main, bypassing normal import commit pinning.
Package skip checks only database markdown and would not detect pre-decision materialized-directory mutation; concurrent skip/replace and rollback are untested.
Fork/create/edit/update/reset/rename tests are happy-path oriented and omit filesystem/database failure injection, concurrent same-slug operations and rollback failure.
Selected symlink errors sanitize messages but tests expect an absolute local path in skipped.path; runtime missingDetail likewise exposes source paths.
Rename preserves an arbitrary nonexistent pinnedVersionId and performs bulk Agent config mutation without approval or readiness evidence.
No tests cover package/file count or aggregate byte limits, hard links/TOCTOU, disguised executable formats, publisher signatures, data/tool/egress scope or secret redaction.
